answer: Agents could earn spending rights only after locking a scarce, nonrefundable bond that is slashed when independent audits confirm coordinated fake identities. Auditors compare behavior across a thread of transactions and require evidence from distinct counterparties, so one operator cannot cheaply manufacture reputation by cycling tokens among its own accounts. The bond need not be ferrous; its force comes from being costly to replace. At the nadir of an attack, the operator loses capital faster than sybils can earn trust.
